newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: ISO sees sugar price dip now, new season recovery.
newsitem.headline: ISO sees sugar price dip now, new season recovery.

text.p: High carryover stocks from the current sugar year are likely to depress prices going into 1997/98 before an eventual recovery, the International Sugar Organization's chief economist said.
The ISO's Tony Hannah said raw sugar prices, weighed by an expected surplus of over two million tonnes in the 1996/97 crop year, were likely to bottom at 10 cents a lb.
The benchmark July futures contract closed at 11.16 cents a lb in New York on Tuesday.
"I think there could be a little bit more pressure on prices...until the start of the new crop cycle in October," Hannah told Reuters in an interview at the ISO's member meeting in Mauritius.

The ISO said earlier this month that a surplus of 2.29 million tonnes was expected in 1996/97 (October-September) and that world export availability in the same period could exceed import demand by 1.88 million tonnes.
Adding to this, exportable but unsold sugar could propel beginning stocks at the start of the new crop cycle as high as 42.8 million tonnes, or 35 percent of world consumption.
However, the surpluses of the past two years were seen meeting greater consumption demand in the forthcoming season, with a recovery in prices following close behind, Hannah said.
"What we will see maybe in 1997/98 is production and consumption the same, or even consumption slightly higher than production. Prices will then recover...," he said.

The ISO's latest world sugar estimate for the 1996/97 season shows a dip in production to 123.49 million tonnes raw value, down on the year before's 124.19 million. Consumption was expected to rise to 121.20 million tonnes from 118.66 milion in 1995/96. -- Nicole Mordant
